chunk_findings.detail: The old implementation built the knob set from `dataclasses.fields(cls)`, so the function itself guaranteed that every `Knobs` field was populated from the corresponding `remote_*` config value (or failed loudly if that value was absent). The new explicit call no longer keeps that promise: if `Knobs` gains a field with a default, e.g. `max_lanes: int = 1`, and `Config.swarm` exposes `remote_max_lanes=5`, `from_config` returns `max_lanes=1` and silently ignores the configured knob. The comment says a test holds the field/knob lists together, but the production path can still be wrong whenever that test is not updated or not run; the change replaces a runtime invariant with a manual list.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote_config.py:from_config

chunk_findings.detail: The new `prices.limit` and `prices.reset` entries make the dead-knob ratchet pass on a hard-coded allowlist without verifying the claimed reads. If `services/limit_routing.headroom` is changed so it no longer calls `PricesConfig.limit_of`/`reset_of` (or calls them only on a default `PricesConfig` rather than loaded config), `test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py` still passes because the names are exempted in this file, while the corresponding config knobs are actually dead. The comment’s “Pinned by tests/test_limit_routing.py” promise is not enforced by this test, so the ratchet can falsely report no dead knobs.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not actually pin that `PricesConfig.limit_of` / `reset_of` read `self.limit` / `self.reset`; it only checks that they return the same constants it just set. chunk_findings.detail: The new test claims to pin the `KNOWN_UNREAD` exemption by proving that `PricesConfig.limit_of` and `reset_of` read `self.limit` and `self.reset`, but it only assigns one value to each field and checks that the accessors return the corresponding hard-coded expected values. If `limit_of` is mutated to `return 5.0` and `reset_of` to `return "1d"` unconditionally, the test still passes even though neither accessor reads the config knobs anymore, and the dead-knob ratchet would still accept the `prices.limit` / `prices.reset` exemption. Thus the added test does not actually pin the claimed reads and the exemption can still outlive the read.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_prices_accessors_read_the_knobs` still does not pin that `limit_of` / `reset_of` read `self.limit` / `self.reset`. Distinct per-model returns and an unknown-model case kill a constant return, but a function that ignores the knobs and hardcodes the literals this test just wrote still passes, for example `limit_of` returning `{"a": 5.0, "b": 7.0}.get(model)` and `reset_of` returning `{"a": "1d", "b": "2d"}.get(model, "1mo")`. With that implementation `prices.limit` and `prices.reset` are unread, so the `KNOWN_UNREAD` exemption stays false while the ratchet stays green. A second assignment of different maps (and a re-check that the new values and the new misses come back) is what would force a live read.
